Style cells by column, in the header, or by a condition

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_cell_style.Rd

plan_cell_style() says how cells look — bold, italic, underline, colour, background, alignment, indent, border — and which cells: the column header (header = TRUE), whole columns (cols), or the rows a condition chooses (where, or an attribute written as a formula). It is SAS's call define() in a compute block: a cell looks at its own row and decides how it is printed. Columns are named, so a reordered table keeps its styles; the styles run on the pages in the order written.

Usage

plan_cell_style(
  .plan,
  cols = NULL,
  header = FALSE,
  where = NULL,
  bold = NULL,
  italic = NULL,
  align = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  background = NULL,
  border = NULL,
  underline = NULL,
  indent_twips = NULL
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

cols

The columns styled, by name (.values for every value column); left out, every column.

header

TRUE styles the column header (style_header()) instead of the body; it takes bold, italic, underline, align and border, and no where.

where

A one-sided formula over the table's columns choosing the rows, where = ~ is.na(label); the attributes given apply there and leave the other rows alone. Left out, the whole of cols is styled (style_cols()).

bold, italic, align, color, background, underline

How the cells look. Each is one of:

a value

bold = TRUE, align = "center", color = "#CC0000": applied to the cells cols / header / where choose.

a one-sided formula

the value computed row by row over the table's columns, NA leaving the column default alone: bold = ~ is.na(label). A call whose attributes are formulas takes neither where nor header.

a named list of formulas

one a column, by name: color = list(Placebo = ~ ifelse(n > 50, "#CC0000", NA)).

A formula sees the printed rows only with plan_stub(before = TRUE).

border

A column's border, an rtf_border(): on whole columns or the header, not with where.

indent_twips

The left indent of the cells' text, style_cols()'s indent_twips (not on the header).

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; plan_style() for the whole table's look.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

tbl <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Subjects", "Age, mean (SD)", "Female, n (%)"),
  Placebo   = c("86", "75.2 (8.59)", "53 (61.6)"),
  Active    = c("84", "75.7 (8.29)", "50 (59.5)"))

# Minimal: the active arm's column in bold
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_cell_style(cols = "Active", bold = TRUE) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]$col_spec[[3]]$bold
#> [1] TRUE

# The header in bold, the arms centred, the count row in italics and
# the active arm's female cell in red
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("Parameter", "Placebo", "Active"))) |>
  plan_cell_style(header = TRUE, bold = TRUE) |>
  plan_cell_style(cols = c("Placebo", "Active"), align = "center") |>
  plan_cell_style(where = ~ Parameter == "Subjects", italic = TRUE) |>
  plan_cell_style(color = list(
    Active = ~ ifelse(startsWith(Parameter, "Female"), "#CC0000", NA))) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ────────────────────────────────────────
#> Parameter         Placebo      Active   
#> ────────────────────────────────────────
#> Subjects            86           84     
#> Age, mean (SD)  75.2 (8.59)  75.7 (8.29)
#> Female, n (%)    53 (61.6)    50 (59.5) 
#> 
#> <rtftable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Parameter | Placebo | Active
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>   Cell styles: set (3 rows)
#>
